Article Title: PM Modi to meet Putin on SCO summit sidelines during Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1, the ministry of external affairs said on Thursday.During his four-day visit, PM Modi will undertake a bilateral visit to Tashkent and participate in the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek.PM Modi will also hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. According to news agency PTI, Putin will also be among the leaders with whom PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings on the margins of the summit.PM Modi is also expected to visit the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.This will be PM Modi's fourth visit and his second bilateral visit to Uzbekistan, according to MEA Secretary (West) Sibi George.Addressing a special briefing on the Prime Minister's visit, MEA Secretary (West) said India and Uzbekistan have maintained "extensive and fruitful engagements" over the years in both bilateral and multilateral formats.Highlighting the depth of economic ties, the MEA Secretary said India is among Uzbekistan's top 10 trading partners, with bilateral trade and investments together close to USD 1 billion."We have wide-ranging cooperation in the fields of critical minerals, pharma, education, information technology, and the health sector," he said.The summit coincides with the SCO's 25th anniversary of its founding. After serving as an observer since 2005, India became a full member of the organisation in 2017.From August 31 to September 1, the Prime Minister will visit Bishkek, George stated.According to the MEA, the organisation's main goal was to combat the three "evils" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to present challenges.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1. PM Modi will undertake a bilateral visit to Tashkent and participate in the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing assembly convention on Thursday when he left his designated chair and took a seat alongside ministers in the front row during the afternoon session. It was unusual for a chief minister to occupy a seat meant for ministers, news agency PTI reported citing a source.Vijay, who normally sits in a separate chair positioned close to Speaker J C D Prabhakar, moved across the front row and sat between ministers K A Sengottaiyan, who is also the leader of the House, and Aadhav Arjuna.The move drew attention as chief ministers traditionally occupy a separate designated seat in the House, while ministers sit alongside them according to seniority.Members of the House occasionally change seats briefly to interact with colleagues. However, Vijay's move was notable because he shifted from his official chair and remained seated among the ministers.The chief minister had attended government programmes earlier in the day and arrived at the assembly for the later session.The 234-member Tamil Nadu assembly follows a conventional seating arrangement in which the chief minister occupies a designated chair near the Speaker, while ministers are seated separately in the front row.The opposition leaders sit across from the treasury benches, with their respective party members seated behind them.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing assembly convention. He left his designated chair and took a seat alongside ministers in the front row. It was unusual for a chief minister to occupy a seat meant for ministers.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Thursday questioned what he described as conflicting statements by senior military officials on the extent of cooperation between Pakistan and China during Operation Sindoor Sharing video clips on X, Ramesh said Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen Rahul Singh had, on July 4, 2025, highlighted what he called the “very disturbingly deep nature” of the Pakistan-China partnership during the military operation.The Congress leader contrasted those remarks with comments made by former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan on August 25, 2026, saying Chauhan's account appeared to be “simply opposite” to that of Lt. Gen. Singh.“On July 4 2025, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen Rahul Singh had revealed the very disturbingly deep nature of the Pakistan-China jugalbandi during Operation Sindoor. On Aug 25, 2026, the former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan made his own revelations on this jugalbandi - which are simply opposite to what Lt. Gen Singh had said. The nation is confused," said Ramesh on X.The Congress leader questioned whether the differing accounts reflected a broader effort to shape the public narrative around India's relations with China.“What is going on here? Is there some deeper plan to change the narrative?” he asked.He also linked the issue to the Centre's broader China policy, alleging that there had been a “calibrated capitulation to China” and citing what he described as the Prime Minister's “infamous clean chit to China on June 2020” as well as India's record trade deficits with China.Ramesh's remarks came ex-CDS Chauhan, speaking at the ‘VIMARSH’ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekananda International Foundation, said Pakistan had failed to obtain evidence of the targets struck by India despite attempts to access commercial satellite imagery.Chauhan said the presence of Chinese personnel supporting Pakistan's military equipment during Operation Sindoor should be viewed in the context of "contractual obligations", while cautioning against drawing conclusions beyond established facts.In the clip shared by Ramesh, General Singh can be heard stating that the key lessons from Operation Sindoor were that India faced a multi-adversary challenge, with Pakistan at the forefront and China and Turkey providing significant military support. He added that China also used the conflict to assess its weapons and systems in a real-world environment.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, days after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people. The operation targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK).
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned what he described as conflicting statements by senior military officials. NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan, which is protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at the national capital's Jantar Mantar.In a social media post on X, Nadda said that he met Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan as per the pre-determined schedule, adding that another meeting will be held soon."Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on August 21, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Shri Harsh Dubey, Shri Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Shri Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," he said.However, Nadda did not give details of the meeting.Meanwhile, Harsh Dubey said that the meeting was an important step towards dialogue."Positive initiative for the welfare of all society today. Our team met with the honourable Shri JP Nadda Ji. During this time, there was a brief discussion with him regarding the demonstration that took place on August 21. This meeting is an important step towards dialogue.We will soon meet again with the honourable Nadda Ji and strive to move forward with a positive and just decision in the interest of all society," Dubey said."Our objective is not against any section, but rather to democratically and peacefully present our views for equal opportunities, a just system, and necessary reforms in the national interest. Further information and decisions regarding this will be officially communicated shortly," he added.Reservation Hatao Andolan is demanding that quotas in academics and employment should strictly be determined by income levels rather than social or caste identities. Additionally, the protesters advocated for a "one family, one reservation" policy and demanded the immediate withdrawal of the UGC's 2026 caste-equity directives.A large number of people gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Friday to protest against caste-based reservation, following which the Delhi Police and Central Forces were deployed at the protest site to maintain law and order.Security personnel were seen present at Jantar Mantar as protesters assembled at the designated protest area. The police deployment was carried out as a precautionary measure amid the large gathering.Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) is an official Instagram page with 5.6 million followers. The platform rapidly gained traction by adopting the protest-mobilisation tactics of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and has now called for a physical protest against the reservation system.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan. Protesters are protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at Jantar Mantar. Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan met with the minister.

Article Title: Delhi HC quashes criminal defamation case against senior advocate Pinaki Misra
Article Text:
The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra

New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra, in a case alleging that he had said certain objectionable words about a lawyer in an interview.The high court also quashed a trial court's April 2019 order summoning Misra to face trial for defamation, saying permitting the proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice.Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said the complainant had examined himself as the sole witness and had not provided any material to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had lowered his reputation in others' estimation."There is no material on record, in the form of statement of any other person or otherwise, to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had the effect of lowering the reputation of Respondent No 2 (complainant) in the estimation of others."The allegation that the publication caused damage to his reputation, by itself, remains an assertion of the complainant and does not establish the statutory requirement contemplated by Explanation 4 to Section 499 (defamation) of IPC," the court said in its order passed on August 25.The high court said permitting the criminal proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice and instead subject the petitioner (Misra) to the rigours of a criminal trial in the absence of sufficient foundational material."Accordingly, this court deems it appropriate, in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC, to quash the impugned summoning order and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom. The petition is accordingly allowed," it said.It was alleged that the complainant advocate had filed a complaint with the Bar Council of Delhi in 2018 against Misra, alleging that the senior advocate's appearance on behalf of power distribution companies before the National Green Tribunal amounted to professional misconduct.After the dispute was reported in a newspaper, it was alleged that Misra gave an interview to another newspaper in which he purportedly used certain objectionable words against the complainant.The complainant filed two defamation complaints alleging that Misra's objectionable remarks have lowered his reputation in the eyes of the public and also affected his professional life.The high court, in its order, noted that the allegation against Misra was founded upon the contents of an online news report.It said Misra had specifically denied having given the interview and had communicated in March 2019 to the editor of the news establishment, denying that he gave the alleged interview and seeking the publication's clarification.The court said the alleged imputation was founded upon an online news report, which has not been supported by examination of the concerned reporter, author, editor or any other person associated with the news portal, particularly when the petitioner had specifically denied having made the alleged statement and had also sent a communication seeking clarification in this regard.PTI
Article Summary: Delhi High Court quashes criminal defamation proceedings against Pinaki Misra. Case alleged he had said certain objectionable words about a lawyer in an interview. High court also quashed a trial court's April 2019 order summoning Misra to face trial for defamation.

Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet. India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas.

Article Title: 'Issue of enormous significance': Kharge writes to PM Modi, demands 25-year delimitation freeze
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, reiterating the Congress' demand to maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 for another 25 years.Kharge's letter came after Union parliamentary affairs minister hinted at a possible special session of Parliament for the passage of the Delimitation Bill.In his letter, Kharge urged the government to convene an all-party meeting to discuss its proposed delimitation exercise before any such session."I have written to PM Modi on delimitation, the delay in prorogation of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, and the likely special session mentioned by the Union minister of parliamentary affairs in a television interview last evening," Kharge said."I had last written to you on July 16, 2026 requesting you to convene an All-Party meeting for discussing the Government's proposals for delimitation. I had also requested you to give all political parties adequate time to study such proposals in detail before they are introduced in any special session of Parliament that you may be contemplating," he added.Kharge also urged PM Modi to maintain the state-wise strength in Lok Sabha for another 25 years and introduce one-third reservation for women from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections."Maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 for another 25 years; Maintain the existing state-wise strength in the Lok Sabha for another 25 years; "Introduce one-third reservation for women from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.Kharge reiterated his demand that the government convene an all-party meeting and give political parties and state governments adequate time to examine the proposals."This is an issue that has enormous significance for the country. Please do not again try and bulldoze as you attempted on April 16 and 17, 2026," Kharge said.
Article Summary: Kharge's letter came after Union parliamentary affairs minister hinted at a possible special session of Parliament for the passage of the Delimitation Bill. In his letter, Kharge urged the government to convene an all-party meeting to discuss its proposed delimitation exercise before any such session.

Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan. The scheme is aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.

Article Title: Caste count method in Census ‘misleading’: Congress letter to PM
Article Text:
The letter from Kharge and Rahul said govt should prepare a fresh questionnaire through consultations with parties.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Terming the methodology for caste count adopted in Census 2027 “misleading” as it will not give a headcount of OBCs, leaders of opposition in Parliament, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, have written to PM Narendra Modi demanding the Census questionnaire on caste notified recently be abandoned and a new one be drafted. They underlined that the word “OBC” has not even been used in the Census.In the backdrop of the controversy triggered by the questionnaire, Kharge and Rahul told the PM “your govt” has adopted an “open-ended question” to collect information about caste, and enumerators will have to take for an answer whatever a person replies to the caste question. They argued that a caste is known by different names and sub-castes depending on the region, which would result in one caste being recorded by thousands of names. “This would result in lakhs of castes being registered in the country, and the entire data recorded in the caste census would become useless,” the letter said.“We don’t approve of the caste census being done through this methodology. Govt should cancel the present questionnaire and prepare a fresh one through consultations with political parties, experts, and the public so that a correct headcount of every caste and community is collected and the caste census is precise, relevant, and beneficial,” it said.It said a readymade solution to the problem is that a “drop-down menu” comprising a list of castes be added to the questionnaire. “This very methodology is used for counting SCs and STs (in Census)... This methodology was adopted in the surveys of Bihar and Telangana. We are enclosing the caste lists of the two surveys for understanding.” Further, the letter said such a list of castes for Census can easily be compiled on the basis of the existing Socially and Educationally Backward Classes list and data from the Anthropological Survey of India.Releasing the letter, AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh and OBC department chairperson Anil Jaihind said govt had, in an affidavit to SC in Sept 2021, submitted that a “drop-down menu” with a list of castes will have to be used if a caste census were to be done. Ramesh said census enumerators can carry the said list of OBCs and record precise answers. He accused govt of “sabotaging” the caste census.
Article Summary: Leaders of opposition in Parliament, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, have written to PM Narendra Modi. They underlined that the word "OBC" has not even been used in the Census. They argued that a caste is known by different names and sub-castes depending on the region, which would result in one caste being recorded by thousands of names.

Article Title: ‘Jhooth ki goonj’ site ‘fact-checks’ Rahul’s student meet claims

NEW DELHI: With Rahul Gandhi looking to ride on the impact of his ‘Chhatron ki goonj’ initiative in his campaign against govt, a website, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, claiming to fact-check his assertions at the four editions of the event so far, has been grabbing attention in saffron circles.The digital counterpunch against Rahul’s campaign obviously complements BJP ’s efforts, but the party has denied any association with the website. The website itself makes no direct mention of the people behind it, but as it trended on social media, some attributed its creation to “nationalist researchers” and Gen Z-ers, the very generation Rahul is targeting in his hops across cities.“Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads, making no secret of where it stands in his pitch against BJP. It says Rahul has made 40 claims in his four interactions, and all of them were either false or misleading (29 false and 11 misleading).It adds that Rahul had said that out of 1,000 youths looking for jobs, about 36 will get permanent jobs. Roughly, 300 will remain unemployed and about 700 will become gig workers, he said. Rejecting the claim as false, the website cites PLFS unit-level data to claim that 26 out of every 100 graduates aged 15-29 in 2025 have salaried jobs.Taking on another claim that Rahul had made — about 29% women faced physical violence — the website says he relied on old NFHS data. “Since the Modi govt came to office, the NFHS data shows a clear decline in spousal physical and/or sexual violence: from 37.2% in (2005-06) to 22.3% in (2023-24),” it says.How much impact the website will make is anyone’s guess, but it has certainly got pro-BJP voices on social media excited. “From tweaked numbers to fabricated stats, every single claim has now been fact-checked,” one user said.
Article Summary: “Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads. It says Rahul has made 40 claims in his four interactions, and all of them were either false or misleading (29 false and 11 misleading)

Article Title: Flood-rescued elephant Joymoti airlifted and shifted to Anant Amabani’s Vantara for specialised care
Article Text:
Ensuring the highest standards of welfare during air transport

Joymoti’s story highlights the need for specialised veterinary care facilities closer to where wildlife emergencies occur

Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant rescued from the devastating floods in Nagaland and Assam in July, was airlifted and moved to Vantara, Jamnagar, where she has already begun receiving immediate and specialised veterinary treatment.The elephant was swept away by floodwaters in Nagaland during the second week of July and was subsequently rescued by local communities with the assistance of government agencies. She sustained multiple injuries during the incident, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen, as well as a deep, maggot-infested wound around her external genital area. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing. She also has longstanding lameness in her left hind leg, resulting from a fracture sustained during logging, which affects her ability to walk normally and access food and water.Following her rescue, Joymoti received first aid and primary veterinary care locally, including wound dressing, pain medication, multivitamin and mineral supplements and supportive treatment. However, given the severity and multiple locations of her injuries, her advancing age and existing mobility challenges, she requires immediate treatment in a specialised hospital setting.Joymoti's transfer to Vantara is solely for immediate and specialised veterinary treatment. The decision to airlift her has been taken with her welfare and medical needs at the centre, allowing her to reach a specialised elephant hospital while minimising the duration and physical demands of ground transportation. Upon arrival at Vantara, Joymoti will undergo a comprehensive veterinary assessment and receive specialised treatment for her injuries and eye condition, along with nutritional and supportive care as required.Transporting an elephant by air for specialised hospital care is an unusual undertaking in India, requiring extensive veterinary, animal-care and logistical planning. Joymoti's transfer is being planned and carried out with careful attention to her health, comfort and safety at every stage, from her veterinary assessment and preparation before travel to loading, monitoring during the flight and her arrival at the hospital.Air transport can significantly reduce the duration of a long-distance journey for an animal requiring urgent medical attention. For elephants with serious injuries, chronic health conditions or mobility challenges, reducing journey time and avoiding prolonged ground travel can be an important consideration in protecting their welfare.Joymoti’s case also highlights the importance of having specialised elephant veterinary care facilities closer to areas where elephants are affected by floods, human-wildlife conflict and other health emergencies.Vantara has proposed the establishment of three wildlife veterinary care centres in Assam, including a dedicated centre for elephants, to strengthen local capacity for wildlife emergency veterinary care. The proposed centres would include species-specific facilities and veterinary support, enabling animals in need to receive timely and appropriate treatment closer to where emergencies occur. The centres would be operated completely independently by the Assam Forest Department.The aim is to strengthen local capacity so that elephants and other wildlife in Assam can receive high-quality care closer to home, avoiding the need for long-distance transportation whenever specialised treatment is required.Joymoti’s journey to Vantara is not a permanent relocation, but an urgent medical transfer undertaken solely to provide the specialised lifesaving treatment she currently requires. Her case underscores the importance of strengthening local veterinary capacity while ensuring that animals requiring advanced care can access it safely and without delay. At Vantara, the immediate priority is to provide Joymoti with the specialised treatment she needs and the best possible chance of recovery and a healthy, safe and dignified life.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.

Article Title: Low beam by default: Centre to tighten headlamp norms
Article Text:
CURBING THE GLARE: The steps target a major cause of crashes — high beams can briefly blind motorists coming from opposite direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From next April, automatic headlamps in new two-wheelers will work only in passing beam (low beam) mode, and headlamps of cars and other vehicles will have less intense illumination to reduce glare considering that such lights cause visual discomfort or impairs the vision of other road users.The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules. The amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made because efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.At present, the Automatic Headlamp On (AHO) system can switch on both low beam and high beam modes depending on vehicle settings. The proposed rule mandates that when the automatic system is active, the headlamp will be on low beam.As for high-intensity headlamps, the maximum permissible intensity has been reduced from 1.5 lakh candela or cd (official base unit of luminous intensity) to 1 lakh cd for two-wheelers.The maximum permissible intensity for four-wheelers (cars) has been reduced from 2.25 lakh cd to 1.5 lakh cd.Studies show that white light emitted from headlamps and front fog lamps with higher colour temperatures cause significant glare, leading to discomfort and reduced visibility for other road users. To address this issue, the maximum permissible colour temperature has been restricted to 6,500 Kelvin (K).It has also been proposed that the mounting height of main-beam headlamps be equivalent to that prescribed for passing-beam headlamps.These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India — drivers using headlamps on high beam in urban areas, which can temporarily blind motorists approaching from the opposite direction, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of crashes.TOI has learnt the new-generation system will also include an audio alert to discourage unnecessary use of high-beam mode on city roads. If a driver manually switches to high beam in urban conditions, the vehicle will prompt them to shift back to low beam.However, the alert will be speed sensitive. Drivers travelling on highways at speeds above 60 kmph won’t receive the warning, since the use of high-beam mode may be necessary on poorly illuminated highway stretches. The feature is intended to promote safer driving behaviour in urban areas while ensuring that highway driving is not adversely affected, officials said.
Article Summary: From next April, automatic headlamps in new two-wheelers will work only in passing beam (low beam) mode. Headlamps of cars and other vehicles will have less intense illumination to reduce glare. These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India.

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force. “Why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other” he said.

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.

Article Title: Beyond Ayodhya and the fish row: Why Nishad vote matters in Uttar Pradesh 2027 battle
Article Text:
The Nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in Ayodhya ahead of 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.

At a time when many Hindu devotees traditionally give up non-vegetarian food during 'Sawan', fish has acquired an unlikely political importance in Uttar Pradesh.The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.But behind the sparring over what was - or was not - on Rai's plate lies a larger electoral calculation. The Nishad vote has shifted political loyalties before, and with the BJP seeking to retain its non-Yadav OBC coalition and the opposition trying to prise open that support, the community could once again become an important factor in the 2027 contest.The controversy began earlier this month when Sanjay Nishad said at a programme: "Bina lahsun-pyaz ki bani machhli shakahari hai."The remark came during Sawan, a month when many Hindu devotees observe dietary restrictions, and quickly attracted attention because of the community he represents. Nishads have historically depended on rivers and water bodies for fishing, fish-rearing, boating and related livelihoods, making food and fishing practices part of a broader social and economic identity.Then came Ayodhya.On August 23, UP Congress president Ajay Rai travelled to Tarun, around 30 km from Ayodhya, after visiting Hanumangarhi, reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and offering prayers at the Ram temple. He attended a programme organised by members of the Nishad community. A video showing fish being prepared at the venue subsequently surfaced.The timing and location gave the BJP an opening.BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary described the alleged fish feast as "highly condemnable and unforgivable", while Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Rai of "duplicity" for visiting a temple and then attending a fish feast during Sawan."You saw the conduct of the Congress state president yesterday. He goes to Hanumangarhi for darshan and, after coming out, enjoys a fish feast and then shouts 'Ram-Ram'," Adityanath said.Rai denied eating fish and challenged the CM to produce evidence. "If he can produce any pictures, I will be ready to resign immediately," he said.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera defended the hosts, saying they belonged to the Nishad community and had their own traditions of eating and drinking.Later, cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar entered the controversy, backing Nishad's earlier claim and asking Congress to clarify whether the fish allegedly served at the event had been cooked with garlic and onion."Sanjay Nishad machhli ke mahir hain, unhe zyada jaankari hai, hum thode kam hain," Rajbhar said.The political argument, however, goes well beyond the menu at one event. The larger story is the political importance of the community that hosted it.The Nishads are a cluster of riverine communities whose traditional livelihoods have been closely tied to rivers, ponds and other water bodies. Community organisations have increasingly used the term 'jal kisan', or water farmers, to describe this relationship.Fishing, fish-rearing, boating and the sale of fish have historically been central to these communities' economic lives. Questions over access to water bodies, fishing rights, sand mining and regulation of traditional occupations therefore have a direct political resonance.The term Nishad is also used as an umbrella for several communities and sub-castes, including Mallah, Kewat, Bind, Kashyap, Dhimar, Batham, Kahar, Manjhi and Turaha. Not all of these communities necessarily identify themselves as Nishad in the same way.In Uttar Pradesh, Nishads are classified among the Other Backward Classes (OBCs).Political estimates put the core Nishad population at around 4.5-5 per cent of the state's electorate. Estimates that include a wider set of related riverine communities put their combined share considerably higher.There is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure, but the community's electoral importance comes less from its statewide percentage than from its concentration.Nishad voters have a significant presence across the Ganga-Yamuna belt and eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia, Mau, Ghazipur, Mirzapur, Bhadohi, Jaunpur and Prayagraj, besides parts of Sultanpur and Fatehpur.The community is considered electorally influential in more than 160 Assembly constituencies, with around 80 seats often identified as having a particularly substantial Nishad presence.That geographical concentration explains why a community accounting for a relatively small share of the state's electorate can command such political attention.The Nishad political identity is also deeply connected to stories from the Hindu epics.In the Ramayana, Nishadraj Guha, the boatman-king, is described as an ally of Ram during his exile. Guha receives Ram, Sita and Lakshman and helps them cross the Ganga.For the Nishad community, the story has long been invoked as a marker of their place within the Ram narrative — not as an identity created by contemporary politics, but as an older cultural association that acquired renewed political meaning during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.The community also invokes Ekalavya from the Mahabharata, who is traditionally identified as belonging to the Nishad community. His story - of a skilled archer seeking to learn from Dronacharya and ultimately giving his thumb as guru dakshina - has come to represent a different strand of Nishad memory: talent, exclusion and the struggle for recognition.The two figures capture contrasting elements of the community's epic imagination: Nishadraj represents proximity to and loyalty towards Ram, while Ekalavya represents ability denied recognition.These narratives have subsequently been woven into the community's assertion of a distinct historical and social identity.Sections of the community found their cultural resonance in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.As the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya gathered momentum in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Nishad organisations and leaders participated in the wider mobilisation. The story of Nishadraj Guha gave the movement an immediate cultural connection for sections of the community, while the broader call for 'Ram Rajya' resonated with those who saw the temple campaign as a civilisational and cultural cause.The political landscape changed sharply after BJP leader LK Advani's Ram Rath Yatra in 1990, which transformed the temple issue into a mass political movement. The demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992, further entrenched Ayodhya as a defining issue in BJP politics.As the BJP expanded its support among non-Yadav OBC communities, sections of the Nishad community also moved towards the party.But that support did not become a permanent political contract.Among sections of Nishad political opinion, a recurring grievance emerged: the community had supported the Ram movement but did not receive a commensurate political return.The complaint has, at various points, extended to BJP leaders associated with the Ram movement, including Advani and former UP CM Kalyan Singh, with Nishad voices arguing that their support for the Ram cause did not translate into adequate representation or resolution of longstanding demands regarding representation and farming on the riverside.In the coming years, the same community that participated in the Ram movement subsequently moved towards the Samajwadi Party, created its own political organisation and entered into an alliance with the BJP.That fluidity became particularly visible in the 1990s.Before the emergence of the Nishad Party, the strongest political association for sections of the community came through the social-justice politics of the Samajwadi Party.Phoolan Devi became the most recognisable symbol of that phase.A Mallah woman from Uttar Pradesh, Phoolan Devi contested the Mirzapur Lok Sabha seat on an SP ticket in 1996 and won. She retained the seat in 1999.Her rise gave the community an unusually prominent political figure and turned caste identity into a language of representation.Her political legacy continues to be invoked in Uttar Pradesh.The next major shift came in 2016, when Sanjay Nishad founded the Nirbal Indian Shoshit Hamara Aam Dal, popularly known as the Nishad Party.The party sought to consolidate riverine communities and give political expression to demands involving reservation, representation, fishing rights and livelihoods.Its first major electoral breakthrough came in an unlikely place.In the March 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha bypoll, Praveen Nishad, Sanjay Nishad's son, contested as an SP-backed candidate and defeated the BJP.The result was politically significant because Gorakhpur had been Yogi Adityanath's parliamentary stronghold for five consecutive terms.The defeat demonstrated that the BJP's support among non-Yadav OBC communities could be disrupted when Nishad mobilisation combined with the SP's wider social coalition.But the equation soon changed again.Before the 2019 Lok Sabha election, the Nishad Party moved into the BJP-led NDA. Praveen Nishad joined the BJP and contested the Sant Kabir Nagar Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, winning the election.The BJP-Nishad Party alliance became an important part of the BJP's strategy to consolidate non-Yadav OBC support in eastern Uttar Pradesh.The BJP and Nishad Party continued their alliance into the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.The BJP won 255 seats, while the Nishad Party won six. The NDA retained power with 273 seats in the 403-member assembly.For the BJP, the alliance helped reinforce its eastern Uttar Pradesh coalition.For Sanjay Nishad, however, being part of the government brought a different problem: once an ally enters government, its demands are increasingly judged against what it can actually secure from that government.The biggest unresolved issue remained the demand for Scheduled Caste status for sections of the Nishad community.Sanjay Nishad has repeatedly pressed the BJP government on the demand.On August 18, 2026, just months before the 2027 elections, he escalated the issue again, saying he was prepared to give up his ministerial position if necessary.His friction with the BJP had also become visible after the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when he blamed BJP leaders for his son Praveen Nishad's defeat in Sant Kabir Nagar.Praveen, who contested the seat on a BJP ticket, lost to the Samajwadi Party's Laxmikant Pappu Nishad.The result was another reminder that a BJP-Nishad Party alliance does not necessarily translate into a uniform Nishad vote.That fluidity is what the opposition is trying to exploit ahead of 2027.In March 2026, it appointed Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti as chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Backward Classes Commission. The move came alongside the BJP's continuing alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP responded by appointing Phoolan Devi's sister, 67-year-old Rukmini Devi, as president of the party's Uttar Pradesh women's wing. The appointment was seen as part of Akhilesh Yadav's PDA — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — outreach ahead of the 2027 election.Rukmini Devi subsequently attacked Sanjay Nishad, questioning what he had delivered for the community while being part of the government.The appointments show that the competition for the Nishad vote is not merely about alliances. It is a contest over who represents the community's political memory.Congress, on the other hand, has a more difficult task because its organisational presence among Nishads is weaker.Its August outreach in Tarun was therefore significant. Ajay Rai's visit to the Nishad community programme was an attempt to establish a direct connection with the community.The party's subsequent defence of the event, that the hosts were Nishads with their own food traditions, also allowed Congress to frame the controversy around community identity and traditional livelihoods rather than solely religious conduct.For the SP and Congress, the broader argument is that the Nishad vote is not synonymous with the Nishad Party.The Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP), led by Bihar-based Nishad leader Mukesh Sahani, adds another layer to this contest.VIP entered Uttar Pradesh politics in the 2022 assembly election, seeking support among Nishads and other Extremely Backward Classes, particularly in Purvanchal.The party did not emerge as a major electoral force, but its campaign showed how smaller caste-based parties can complicate a close contest.VIP contested more than 100 seats, primarily in eastern Uttar Pradesh, and said its candidates polled more votes than Congress candidates in 15 constituencies, including Bairia, Bansdih, Phephna, Alapur, Jalalpur, Ghanghata, Balha, Shahganj and Kerakat.Its relationship with the BJP has been politically fluid rather than a straightforward alliance in Uttar Pradesh.Sahani has been a vocal critic of the BJP at various points. However, in neighbouring Bihar where the Nishads remain relevant across the seats in the Ganga area, his political trajectory has repeatedly shifted. VIP contested as part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, switched to the NDA for the 2020 Bihar assembly election (winning 4 seats and entering the cabinet), but was dropped from the NDA in 2022 after contesting against the BJP in UP. In last year's Bihar polls, his party failed to secure any seat.However, in upcoming polls in UP, a few thousand votes in its favour can alter the results in close constituencies.The fish controversy may fade, but the political question it has exposed is unlikely to disappear.The BJP has the advantage of a long association with the Ram movement, an established organisational network and an alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP is seeking to revive the community's social-justice connection through Phoolan Devi's political legacy and the PDA framework.Congress is attempting to build a direct relationship with Nishad voters, while smaller parties such as VIP can potentially fragment the vote.For the Nishads themselves, however, the choice is unlikely to be framed around a single issue.Their political history has moved from the epic memory of Nishadraj and Ekalavya, to participation in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, to the social-justice politics associated with Phoolan Devi, to the rise of the Nishad Party, its alliance with the BJP and subsequent friction over representation and reservation.The lesson from that history is clear: the Nishad vote has never been permanently owned by one party.In 2027, the contest will be over whether Ram and the BJP's organisational alliance can outweigh demands for reservation, representation and livelihoods - and whether the opposition can convert those demands into votes.
Article Summary: The Nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in Ayodhya ahead of 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls. The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a NishadCommunity event, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' scheme and flagged off special buses to provide free travel facilities to women aged 60 years and above in the state.Speaking at the launch event in Lucknow, CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified and strengthening their self-reliance."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government," the Chief Minister said.Under the scheme, women aged 60 years and above will be provided free bus travel facilities. The Chief Minister also said that on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters and daughters would be provided free bus travel along with one accompanying person."The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," CM Yogi said.The Chief Minister said the scheme has been named after Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, whom he described as an exemplary figure of women's self-reliance and good governance."At a time when the country was in the grip of the chaos caused by Mughal invaders, Lokmata Ahilyabai not only achieved the goals of good governance and preserved India's spiritual and cultural heritage but also set an exemplary standard for women's self-reliance," he said.CM Yogi said Ahilyabai Holkar had undertaken the restoration of several temples across the country that had been demolished or damaged by foreign invaders."Whenever the topic of women's self-reliance arises, we all recall the name of Lokmata Ahilyabai with deep reverence and respect," he said.The Chief Minister also launched a sharp attack on the previous governments in the state, alleging that women faced insecurity and lack of dignity before 2017."There was a time before 2017 when a particular slogan echoed among daughters, sisters, and mothers: '" CM Yogi said, referring to the Samajwadi Party.He alleged that the period was marked by concerns over women's safety and a lack of dedicated mechanisms such as integrated helplines, women's beat systems and women's help desks."There was no respect for them, let alone self-reliance; there were no integrated helplines, no women's beat systems, and no women's help desks," he said.CM Yogi further alleged that middlemen controlled pensions and scholarships and that mafia groups exercised influence over sectors including forest, sand, cattle and examination systems."Forest, sand, cattle, and exam-cheating mafias defined the state's identity; a mafia syndicate wielded power parallel to the actual government," he said.The Chief Minister said his government had, for the first time since Independence, formulated a comprehensive action plan aimed at integrating women, who constitute half of society, into governance schemes."This plan encompasses everything from a daughter's birth to her education, employment, and entrepreneurship, while also guaranteeing her safety and dignity; indeed, every scheme, decision, and budget of our government is dedicated to fulfilling these very objectives," he said.The Chief Minister had earlier announced the launch of the scheme in a post on X, saying the initiative was aimed at ensuring convenience and dignity for women."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government. Today in Lucknow, the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' will be inaugurated, under which mothers and sisters of the state aged 60 years and above will be provided with free bus travel facilities," the post read."Additionally, on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters, and daughters will be provided with free bus travel facilities, including one accompanying traveller. The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," he added.The scheme comes as the Uttar Pradesh government seeks to expand measures focused on women's welfare, mobility and self-reliance.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' on Wednesday. Women aged 60+ to get free bus travel under the scheme. CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified.

Article Title: From E coli to amenity gaps: What CAG found beyond the railway makeover
Article Text:
Vande Bharat to E. coli: What CAG found behind Indian Railways’ big makeover (PTI file photo)

Building big, maintaining better

The real makeover begins after inauguration

From showcase projects to everyday reliability

Record capex, heavy government support: The financial reality behind Railways’ makeover
